Lake Arn De Mon (Lycroan: Arandmo) is a freshwater lake located at the western edge of the [[Taiylsh Desert]]. It is the second largest lake in [[Ayuma]], and one of the region's foremost tourist destinations. The [[Elishara River]] provides the largest inflow of water to the lake, and the is the only outflow.

The hilly region of the eastern shore is known both for its historic character and as a major alcohol production region, while the flat weestern shore is known for its resort towns. Lopmao and Dacoingao developed early as resorts for the wealthy, but it was not until the late 16th century when landowners, ruined by [[Lycroan madness]] attacking their alcohol production, began building summer homes to rent out to the burgeoning middle class
==Name==

==Climate==
Lake Arn De Mon affects precipitation in the local area. The area receives approximately 5–7 cm (2–3 in) more precipitation, resulting in more cloudy days and less extreme temperatures. The lake has been seen to freezes over during winters. The microclimate around Lake Balaton has also made the region ideal for viticulture. The Mediterranean-like climate, combined with the soil (containing volcanic rock), has made the region notable for its production of wines since the Roman period 2,000 years ago.
